taxon.identityEvidence: Existing Taal taxonomy review independently matches the accepted WoRMS name and author/year.

sourceFacts.citation: To, D.A.L. et al. (2025). Endangered Species Research 57:177-192. DOI: 10.3354/esr01408.
sourceFacts.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated on the article's final page.
sourceFacts.gutContentSampling: Taal Lake Sardinella tawilis size classes were sampled October 2021-December 2022; no sampling occurred in March-April 2022 during the closed season, and some other trips were postponed.
sourceFacts.stableIsotopeSampling: Pelagic food-web samples were collected in October 2018 and February 2019 at six sites; the SIA sample set included several fish species.
sourceFacts.historicalComparison: The article compares post-eruption 2021-2022 diet findings with pre-eruption diet observations from 2003-2004.
sourceFacts.sampleSize: The paper reports 330 Sardinella tawilis samples in its post-eruption sample and morphometric results.
sourceFacts.dietFinding: The authors describe S. tawilis as size-selective and primarily zooplanktivorous. Copepods and cladocerans were important prey groups; the post-eruption comparison found increased selection for cyclopoid copepods and for Moina micrura, Ceriodaphnia cornuta and Bosmina fatalis, alongside temporal diet shifts.
sourceFacts.interpretationLimit: Food composition varies with period and prey availability. This is a Taal Lake research finding, not a fixed species-wide diet.

accessAndRights.reviewMethod: Official journal PDF link and indexed article text checked; full-text claims cross-checked against the author-shared paper copy and UST institutional research summary. No local source copy retained.
accessAndRights.attribution: Credit all article authors, the original Endangered Species Research publication, DOI and CC BY 4.0; indicate Bangwit's text is paraphrased.
accessAndRights.excludedMaterial: No table or figure image, raw data, coordinates or source prose is copied.

nonClaims: The study does not establish a complete Taal Lake fish list or current presence beyond its sampling period.
A natural diet finding is not bait effectiveness, fishing advice or a catchability prediction.
No diet or presence is inferred for Pansipit River, Cavite, other lakes, or the same fish in a different life stage or season.
nextAction: Continue L1 inland-water coverage with separate locality-resolved fish evidence and rights-cleared diet studies; retain the Taal guide as a source- and period-specific example.
